chapter: On the road with the Moores
title: Backing the Moores as Shorty, Slim and Shorty
summary: Green, J. D. and Harvey perform as backup dancers like the Moores' children, with a small band, on a road show heading back to Texas.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah, it was very illegal. Everyone was hoping to come in, see, and it was being publicized in the newspapers, but it actually never happened, you know. And -- I think it happened a few years later, but this was, as I say, was before Prohibition and -- but you would see these people being jumped, you know, and that song, 'Three O'Clock in the Morning', that was very popular, you know, and 'Sweet Adeline', them as like that, songs, you know. And you ever hear this song, you know somebody been drinking, you see.
How'd you exactly fit into the show? What did you do?
Well, all we did, we -- we did backup, like it was three fellows. She had three children. She had -- we called ourselves Shorty, Slim and Shorty, see, because --
Well, who were you of Shorty, Slim and Shorty?
I was one of the Shorty's.
See, J. D. was Slim, you see, because he was the tallest, and the other playmate, you know, Harvey, he was -- he was the other Shorty.
And he was also a dancer?
So J. D. came along with you on this thing. They asked him to come too?
Okay. And you would do the backup for them. You were like their kids?

It was like a family thing, you see. She had like a pianist, a guitarist and maybe a drummer, something, you know. And see, they was really on their way back to Texas, you see, because, as I said, they wasn't having any more road shows, you know, as they were known as in those days, 1925, you see? What happened there?
